body.text: Can you comfortably handle a hair transplant trip to Istanbul on your own?

Yes, a solo hair transplant trip is straightforward for most healthy adults because you remain awake under local anaesthetic and can walk back to your room after surgery. The main solo risks are poor clinic vetting, rushing airport connections, and bumping freshly placed grafts while tired on the first two nights.

Your biggest safety step happens before booking flights. The [ISHRS Fight the FIGHT campaign](https://fightthefight.ishrs.org/) warns international patients against unlicensed "black-market" operators where non-physicians perform surgical steps. Always verify that your facility holds an official [Turkish Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) and review the [ISHRS tips to avoid bad hair transplant clinics](https://fightthefight.ishrs.org/tips-to-avoid-bad-hair-transplant-clinic/) before committing.
How do airport transfers, hotel room service and Day-2 clinic wash work solo?

Every leg of a 4-day trip works cleanly solo when timed in advance. A private driver meets you at Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), brings you to your hotel, and handles clinic runs on Days 2 and 3. After surgery, rely on 24-hour room service rather than navigating crowded restaurants.

On Day 2 or Day 3—depending on your surgeon's protocol—you return to the clinic for bandage removal and your first supervised wash. Ask the clinic for written, step-by-step home washing instructions and make sure any provided lotions fit under airline 100 ml cabin limits or go into checked baggage.

body.text: What luggage weight limits matter so you don't strain post-op?

Keep your cabin bag under 7–8 kg and avoid lifting anything into overhead aircraft bins for the first week. Bending forward sharply or straining to hoist heavy suitcases raises blood pressure in the scalp, which can trigger bleeding or swelling around freshly implanted grafts.

Pack a four-wheel spinner bag you can push upright rather than pull behind you, or check your main suitcase and travel through the terminal with a small crossbody bag. Book an aisle seat so you do not bump your head on curved window bulkheads, and wear only wide-neck, zip-up, or button-down tops—never pullovers.

items: Pack 4–5 loose button-down or zip-front shirts so nothing touches your scalp.
Bring a U-shaped memory-foam neck pillow to keep your head upright while sleeping.
Keep carry-on weight under 7–8 kg and ask cabin crew or airport porters for lifting help.
Pre-book Istanbul Airport meet-and-assist or buggy service if walking long terminals feels tiring.
Save 112 for emergency ambulance dispatch, per [UK FCDO Turkey Health Advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health).

faq.q: Is 4 days long enough for a hair transplant in Istanbul?
faq.a: For many FUE or DHI trips, 3 to 4 nights covers arrival, surgery, and the first clinic wash. Always confirm the exact post-op clearance day with your licensed medical team before booking return flights.

faq.q: Will I feel dizzy or groggy returning to the hotel alone?
faq.a: Mild fatigue and numbness from local anaesthetic are common after a 6–8 hour session. Using a pre-booked private driver instead of public transport keeps the return trip calm and safe.

faq.q: Can I wear a cap at Istanbul Airport on Day 4?
faq.a: Only wear headgear if your surgeon explicitly approves it. Tight baseball caps can rub or dislodge grafts; most clinics either advise going bareheaded or provide a loose, high-crown fisherman-style hat.

faq.q: How do I sleep alone on the first night without rolling onto grafts?
faq.a: Use two stacked hotel pillows behind your back and a firm U-shaped travel neck pillow around your neck to stay propped at roughly 45 degrees and prevent rolling sideways.

faq.q: Can I bring clinic wash foam and shampoo in my hand luggage?
faq.a: Standard airport security restricts liquids and aerosols to 100 ml containers inside one clear bag. If your clinic provides larger bottles, check a small suitcase or ask for travel-sized decants.
